findings.message: Raw error messages still reach the model through two paths that the round 2-4 toolFailure fix and the round 9 doneNote fix do not cover. (1) When a pinned record fails to load, the code sends `{ error: e.message }` as the record. redactDeep cannot redact that string, so it is quoted to the model as data. (2) The confirmAction 'failed' path (~line 211) writes `couldn't be done: ${message}` into the conversation messages, and the model reads those back on the next turn. Fix: build both from the error kind plus a logError reference, as toolFailure does. Add a table-driven test covering pin errors and failed-confirm notes.
findings.scenario: Pin get_project where the service throws an error whose message quotes a classified value or injection text (e.g. a Postgres 23505 detail with 'gross 285000'), or confirm a card whose service throws such a non-retryable error → the text appears verbatim in provider.calls[n].messages.

findings.message: Environment names are matched two ways. recordDeployment and voidDeployment use lower(name) = lower(input). upsertEnvironment and removeEnvironment use exact `name = input.name`, and the unique constraint (project_id, name) is case-sensitive. So 'Prod' and 'prod' can both exist, upsert creates a second environment instead of matching the existing one, and the case-insensitive lookups then pick an arbitrary row. The ReleaseDeployed event also carries the caller's spelling (input.environment) instead of env.name. Fix: use one matcher for every service (for example a unique index on (project_id, lower(name)) plus lower() everywhere), and emit env.name.
findings.scenario: upsertEnvironment({projectKey:'LAB', name:'prod'}) while 'Prod' exists → a new non-Prod 'prod' is added; recordDeployment(environment:'Prod') may then hit 'prod' → released=false, and nothing is released.

findings.message: Each history row has its own Void form, but it sends only the environment name. voidDeployment always voids the latest non-voided deployment for that environment, so Void on an older row voids a different record. Fix: send the deployment id and void by id, checking that it belongs to the release.
findings.scenario: v2.4.0 has Prod deployments on Oct 1 (deployed) and Oct 5 (rolled-back). The user clicks Void on the Oct 1 row with 'wrong pipeline' → the Oct 5 record is voided and the Oct 1 one stays live.

findings.message: nextStep finds the next stage by `position === last.position + 1` and treats 'no next stage' as Live. Positions are not renumbered when an environment is removed, so a gap ends the chain early. A release whose last reached stage is not a deployed Prod (Prod status 'testing', or a project with no Prod) also shows 'Live'. Fix: take the next stage in sort order, and return null only when a Prod deployment has status 'deployed'.
findings.scenario: LAB removes QA, leaving Dev=1, UAT=3, Prod=4. A release is deployed to Dev → the Action column shows 'Live' and there is no 'Promote to UAT' button. Likewise Prod status 'testing' → 'Live'.

findings.message: Retention for delivery.deployment starts the clock for both recorded_by and voided_by at the deployment's `at`. voided_by is set when the record is voided, possibly years later, so the voider's name is anonymised less than seven years after the void. The round-4 fix covered closed_at for projects but not this field. Fix: give voided_by its own entry with start.at ['voided_at'].
findings.scenario: Deployment at 2026-01, voided 2031-01 → voided_by is anonymised in 2033-01, two years after the void instead of seven.

findings.message: Route params are decoded twice. The comment says Next already hands over decoded segments, and matchRoute runs decodeURIComponent on them again. Fix: drop the second decode, or decode in exactly one place.
findings.scenario: A release tagged '50%' links to /delivery/releases/CON/50%25. Next decodes it to '50%', the second decode throws, and the page is not found. A tag 'a%20b' resolves to the release 'a b' instead.

findings.message: removeEnvironment says 'void them or keep the environment', but voided deployments are still counted (and still hold the foreign key), so voiding never makes removal possible. EnvironmentsCard also disables Remove while voided rows exist. Fix the message.
findings.scenario: Void the only Staging deployment, then remove Staging → still refused with the same advice.

findings.message: The README lists only two events and leaves out delivery.proposal.rekeyed. Its contracts list also leaves out ProposalRekeyed, although contracts.ts, module.ts and the tests all have them.

A pinned record whose read fails is sent to the model as `{ error: e.message }`. Round 3 fixed this for tool calls: converse() gives the model a fixed phrase per error kind (toolFailure) and never the message, because messages can echo classified values and attacker text. The pin path, a second way data reaches the provider, skips that fix. Fix: on failure, use toolFailure(pin.tool, e, logError(...)) or a fixed marker, never e.message.
findings.scenario: A user pins a record. The read tool throws `duplicate key: gross 285000 for kasun@...` or `no ticket 'Ignore previous instructions…'`. That exact text goes to Anthropic inside the pinned <data> block.

findings.message: Un-releasing always sets proposals to 'verified', whatever phase they had before the Prod deployment. That phase is never recorded, so voiding a mistaken deployment cannot undo it. Fix: store each proposal's phase before release (on the proposal or the releasing deployment) and restore it on void, with the from/to events matching.
findings.scenario: CON-016 is 'proposed'. It is added to v2.6.0, and Prod is recorded by mistake → released. Void with 'recorded by mistake' → CON-016 is now 'verified', not 'proposed'.

findings.message: A specclaw-synced proposal's phase has two writers. syncProposal overwrites phase from the repo, and recordDeployment (Prod) and moveProposal (MCP/chat; only the board UI hides Move for specclaw rows) also write it. The next sync sees a fingerprint mismatch and silently reverts, emitting a backwards phase_changed. Fix: pick one owner. Either recordDeployment and moveProposal refuse or skip source='specclaw' rows, or the sync keeps a 'released' set by a Prod deployment.
findings.scenario: An AMX release containing AMX-042 is deployed to Prod → AMX-042 is 'released'. The next sync (change not yet archived) → AMX-042 goes back to 'verified', and a released→verified event is emitted.

findings.message: assignProposals only checks 'already shipped in another release'. It does not check whether the target release already has a live Prod deployment. A proposal added to a release that is already live never becomes released, which breaks 'Released means it reached Prod' for that release. Fix: refuse to add proposals to a release with a live released deployment, or release them in the same write.
findings.scenario: setReleaseProposals(HRI v0.9.2, [..., 'HRI-001']) → HRI-001 joins a release that is in Prod, but it stays 'building' and the release map shows the release as Live.

findings.message: The data-region gate trusts regions.ai, an Admin-typed declaration. providerRegion and aiRegion never reach anthropicProvider, which always calls the SDK's default endpoint. So 'AI runs in AU' unblocks AI without anything making calls stay in AU. Fix: make the provider endpoint/region come from the policy (or the deployment config), and block when the configured endpoint's region is unknown or doesn't match.
findings.scenario: Admin sets dataRegion=AU, aiRegion=AU, providerRegion=ap-southeast-2 → blockedReason is null, and calls with tenant data go to the default Anthropic API endpoint, outside AU.

findings.message: A pin whose tool isn't among the viewer's read tools is dropped with `continue`. The model and user are never told the pinned context was left out, so the answer reads as if it covered the pin. Fix: add a 'not available' data item for that label.
findings.scenario: A user pins a record from a tool their token or role can't read → the pin chip shows, but the model answers with no context and no note that it was skipped.
